articles.title: Almir Rouche, André Rio e mais: veja programação do Bal Masqué 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor pernambucano celebra 40 anos de carreira durante festa. Baile acontece no dia 23 de janeiro, no Clube Internacional.
articles.summary: Festa vai homenagear o cantor pernambucano Almir Rouche, que celebra 40 anos de carreira. O baile acontece no Clube Internacional, na Zona Oeste do Recife, no dia 23 de janeiro.
articles.body:
Foto de arquivo de Almir Rouche — Foto: Luigi Marchi/Divulgação

Um dos tradicionais bailes de carnaval do Recife , o Bal Masqué vai homenagear o cantor pernambucano Almir Rouche na edição que celebra seus 40 anos de carreira, em 2027. A festa será realizada no dia 23 de janeiro, a partir das 16h, no Clube Internacional, no bairro da Madalena, na Zona Oeste da capital (veja programação abaixo) .

Neste ano, o baile retoma o formato “Entardecer no Bal Masqué”, com dois palcos: um dedicado ao frevo e outro ao samba. O encerramento terá show do homenageado Almir Rouche, que se apresenta ao lado de convidados.

No palco "Samba", a apresentação do Sambstar faz uma homenagem a Jamelão do Cavaco, um dos fundadores do grupo, que morreu em 19 de março deste ano, vítima de câncer.

Além dos shows, a programação inclui desfile de fantasias e escolha do Garoto e da Garota Bal Masqué, no palco frevo. O público também poderá visitar uma feira de artesanato com artigos de carnaval e uma praça de alimentação.

Nascido em Igarassu, no Grande Recife, Almir Rouche iniciou a trajetória musical à frente das bandas Pinguim e Banda Humm, entre 1988 e 2000. Há mais de 15 anos, segue em carreira solo.

Entre as músicas mais conhecidas do cantor estão "A vida inteira te amar", "Deusa de Itamaracá" e "Galo, eu te amo".

O artista também foi homenageado pelo carnaval do Recife em 2017 , quando comemorou três décadas de carreira.

Em julho de 2019, o cantor foi surpreendido pelo diagnóstico de um aneurisma cerebral , que se rompeu e exigiu uma cirurgia de emergência. Almir Rouche passou pelo procedimento e, segundo os médicos, não ficou com sequelas.

articles.title: Santiago Peña: Promotores tentam abrir cofre em casa de verão | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta terça (10), equipes voltaram à residência com "o dispositivo correspondente para proceder à abertura", anunciou o Ministério Público.
articles.summary: Nesta terça (10), equipes voltaram à residência com "o dispositivo correspondente para proceder à abertura", anunciou o Ministério Público.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público do Paraguai tentará abrir o cofre de alta segurança que foi encontrado atrás de uma porta escondida na mansão de veraneio do ex-presidente Santiago Peña nesta terça-feira (10), segundo veículos da imprensa local.

O compartimento foi descoberto por policiais e promotores de Justiça durante buscas no local, que fica em San Bernardino, a 50 km de Assunção, no domingo (8). No entanto não foi possível abri-lo.

Nesta terça, equipes voltaram à residência com "o dispositivo correspondente para proceder à abertura", anunciou o Ministério Público, ressaltando a "alta complexidade" do cofre, mas sem informar a metodologia utilizada.

Segundo o jornal paraguaio "ABC", o acesso ao cofre só é possível por um corredor que parte de um dos quartos. A porta, disse o ABC, também é reforçada e possui um sistema de segurança de nível altíssimo, com quatro etapas diferentes para abri-la, incluindo reconhecimento facial ou de íris, impressão digital, PIN e chaves Mul-T-Lock.

Nesta segunda-feira (9), o promotor Christian Benítez declarou à ABC que avaliava solicitar a colaboração de Leticia Ocampos, esposa do ex-presidente, para liberar o acesso mediante reconhecimento biométrico, ou realizar uma detonação controlada.

Buscas em uma das casas de Santiago Peña — Foto: DIVULGAÇÃO / PROCURADORIA-GERAL DO PARAGUAI / AFP

A mansão foi financiada parcialmente por meio de empréstimos do Ueno Bank, cujas parcelas mensais, segundo a investigação, equivaleriam a seis vezes o salário de Peña.

Outra residência de Peña, na capital Assunção, também foi revistada nesta segunda. Os promotores apreenderam documentos, celulares, computadores e gravações de câmeras de segurança.

Também realizaram busca e apreensão em uma sede do banco e na residência do ex-presidente do Banco Central, Carlos Carvallo, que antes integrava o conselho de administração do Ueno Bank e agora está em prisão preventiva.

O Ministério Público anunciou ainda tratativas com autoridades dos Estados Unidos, Luxemburgo e Argentina para rastrear e recuperar possíveis recursos desviados ao exterior.

Relembre a crise que levou à saída de Santiago Peña da Presidência

Santiago Peña, presidente do Paraguai desde 2023 que renunciou ao cargo em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo/File Photo

Peña, de 47 anos, é investigado por ter favorecido a instituição, da qual ele foi acionista até 2025 como integrante de seu grupo controlador, com fundos públicos.

articles.title: Pai de Meghan Markle volta a ser preso após romper tornozeleira | G1
articles.standfirst: Thomas Markle é pai da duquesa de Sussex, casada com o príncipe Harry. Ele foi detido pela 1ª vez na semana passada, por suspeita de posse de material de abuso sexual infantil.
articles.summary: Thomas Markle é pai da duquesa de Sussex, casada com o príncipe Harry. Ele foi detido pela 1ª vez na semana passada, por suspeita de posse de material de abuso sexual infantil.
articles.body:
Thomas Markle , pai da duquesa Meghan Markle, foi preso novamente após romper a tornozeleira eletrônica que usava por determinação da Justiça dos Estados Unidos . Ele havia sido detido na semana passada, suspeito de armazenar materiais de abuso sexual infantil. A nova prisão foi informada pelo Departamento de Justiça nesta terça-feira (10).

▶️ Meghan Markle é a duquesa de Sussex e mulher do príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido . Ela afirmou que está afastada do pai há anos. Relembre mais abaixo.

Thomas, de 82 anos, foi detido pela primeira vez por agentes do FBI na sexta-feira (6) , em Lakeland. Ele vive em um centro de reabilitação desde o fim de 2025, após amputar uma perna.

Horas depois da prisão, um juiz autorizou a liberação de Thomas sob a condição de que ele fosse monitorado com o uso de uma tornozeleira. A Justiça também determinou que ele passasse por uma avaliação de capacidade mental.

Nesta terça-feira, Thomas rompeu o equipamento no início da madrugada e foi preso novamente pouco depois. Segundo Bill Essayli, primeiro assistente do procurador dos EUA, ele estava sob custódia federal à espera de uma audiência em um tribunal de Tampa, na Flórida.

A prisão inicial ocorreu após meses de investigação sobre imagens encontradas em diferentes locais ligados a Markle. Segundo Essayli, aproximadamente 78 itens foram apreendidos em depósitos na região de Los Angeles.

Entre eles estavam slides, negativos de filmes e livros que continham imagens suspeitas de abuso sexual infantil.

As acusações contra Thomas foram divulgadas inicialmente pelo jornal britânico "The Sun", em 23 de outubro. As supostas imagens foram encontradas pelo outro filho dele, Thomas Markle Jr., na antiga casa do pai, nas Filipinas.

Segundo o jornal britânico "Daily Mail", materiais de abuso sexual infantil também foram encontrados em um depósito alugado por Thomas no México.

Thomas Markle, pai da duquesa de Sussex, Meghan Markle. — Foto: Reprodução

Quando as acusações contra o pai vieram a público, Meghan Markle afirmou estar "profundamente abalada" com as suspeitas.

Em um comunicado, a duquesa de Sussex disse que tinha conhecimento das alegações contra Thomas desde 2018. Segundo ela, uma carta enviada à Polícia Metropolitana de Londres e à Proteção da Realeza e de Pessoas Carentes continha acusações "preocupantes" contra o pai.

Meghan afirmou que foi informada de que as suspeitas estavam sendo investigadas e que confiou que as autoridades também estavam protegendo outras famílias.

A duquesa também disse que impediu o contato do pai com os filhos dela e do príncipe Harry — Archie, de 7 anos, e Lilibet, de 5 — para protegê-los.

Meghan não mantém contato com Thomas desde o período que antecedeu o casamento com Harry, em 2018. Dias antes da cerimônia, ele informou que não compareceria por motivos de saúde. Antes disso, havia admitido que posou para fotos de paparazzi.

Alvo de um processo de impeachment , Peña é suspeito de favorecer o banco e chegou a anunciar renúncia, barrada pelo Congresso para evitar que ele mantivesse benefícios. O impeachment foi aprovado, e ele foi detido logo depois .

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV: Peru inaugura maior estátua do mundo para um pontífice | G1
articles.standfirst: Monumento de 14 metros de altura foi inaugurado em Callao, dois dias antes da chegada do pontífice ao país, onde viveu por cerca de 20 anos.
articles.summary: A turnê de 12 dias do papa pela América Latina começou no Uruguai no dia 6 de novembro.
articles.body:
Uma estátua gigante do papa Leão é inaugurada em Callao, no Peru, em 9 de novembro de 2026, às vésperas da visita do pontífice ao país. — Foto: REUTERS/Daniel Becerril

O Peru inaugurou, na segunda-feira (9), uma estátua de 14 metros de altura do papa Leão XIV em Callao, cidade portuária próxima à capital, Lima. Segundo as autoridades locais, o monumento é a maior estátua de um papa no mundo.

A inauguração ocorreu dois dias antes da chegada do pontífice ao país, prevista para quarta-feira (11), na última etapa de sua viagem pela América do Sul.

A escultura retrata Leão XIV com suas tradicionais vestes brancas e um terço no pescoço. Nascido nos Estados Unidos, o papa de 71 anos mantém uma relação próxima com o Peru, onde viveu por cerca de 20 anos, atuou como missionário e foi bispo de Chiclayo, no norte do país, antes de ser nomeado cardeal.

De acordo com estimativas oficiais, o número recorde de mais de 2,5 milhões de fiéis estava concentrado na Avenida do Libertador, no bairro de Palermo, para receber o líder máximo da Igreja Católica.

A turnê de 12 dias pela América Latina começou no Uruguai no dia 6 de novembro. No domingo (8), Leão XIV chegou à Argentina, onde fica até o dia 11. Depois, o pontífice embarcará para o Peru. A visita terminará no dia 17.

Visão de drone da nova estátua do papa Leão, no Peru — Foto: REUTERS/Daniel Becerril

articles.title: Bombeiros do RN lançam campanha natalina para arrecadar brinquedos | G1
articles.standfirst: Doações podem ser entregues até 22 de dezembro em quartéis e unidades da corporação em todo o estado; são aceitos brinquedos novos ou em boas condições de uso.
articles.summary: A campanha de arrecadação de brinquedos dos Bombeiros do RN recebe itens novos e usados em todos os quartéis do estado para presentear crianças até 22 de dezembro.
articles.body:
Campanha recebe doações até 22 de dezembro — Foto: CMBRN/Divulgação

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Rio Grande do Norte (CBMRN) começou nesta terça-feira (10) uma campanha de arrecadação de brinquedos para crianças em situação de vulnerabilidade social. As doações podem ser feitas até 22 de dezembro , em qualquer quartel ou unidade da corporação.

Intitulada “Mãos que Salvam”, a campanha recebe brinquedos novos ou em boas condições de uso. Os itens serão destinados a crianças e famílias atendidas por comunidades e projetos sociais.

Após o período de arrecadação, as equipes dos Bombeiros vão organizar e distribuir os brinquedos. Segundo a corporação, os locais beneficiados serão definidos a partir de um cadastro prévio de comunidades e projetos sociais.

A iniciativa é coordenada pela coronel Denise. Segundo ela, a campanha busca incentivar a solidariedade e aproximar a instituição da população.

“Mais do que arrecadar brinquedos, queremos despertar a solidariedade e mostrar que pequenos gestos podem fazer uma grande diferença na vida de uma criança. Cada doação representa carinho, cuidado e a oportunidade de proporcionar um fim de ano mais feliz para muitas famílias”, afirmou.

articles.title: Scottish boat tour operator fined £2,500 after disturbing dolphins and pilot whales; court hears how his vessel split a pod of up to 25 whales near the coast
articles.summary: Dolphin and pilot whale disturbance convictions against Aberdeen sea life tour operator Richard James Greenhowe have been upheld by the Sheriff Appeal
articles.body: Dolphin and pilot whale disturbance convictions against Aberdeen sea life tour operator Richard James Greenhowe have been upheld by the Sheriff Appeal Court, which refused his appeal on 3 November 2026. Greenhowe, owner and skipper of the sailing vessel Seacab, was found to have deliberately or recklessly disturbed the animals during two separate incidents in July 2023. The judges ruled that everyday language, not scientific terminology, governs what counts as disturbance, because the offence targets what a skipper did and whether it was reckless, so ordinary eyewitness accounts and video footage can prove it without an expert deciding the question.How the Seacab skipper drove through a dolphin feeding area and turned pilot whales towards shoreAccording to the written opinion of the Sheriff Appeal Court, as reported by Scottish Legal News, Greenhowe ran sea life tours from Torry Battery in Aberdeen. On 22 July 2023, dolphins were feeding around the north breakwater at Aberdeen Harbour when Seacab left the harbour, passed the feeding area, turned 180 degrees and travelled back through it, then turned again and made a second pass. At times the boat was between five and 10 metres from the animals. The dolphins head-slapped and then swam out to sea.Eight days later, up to 25 pilot whales, divided into a larger and a smaller pod, were close to the coast. The larger group was moving out to sea when Seacab travelled directly towards it at speed, slowed as it closed in and positioned itself between the whales and open water before turning towards them. The larger pod changed direction and headed for the beach, while the smaller pod became separated. The sheriff treated this as a particular concern because pilot whales close to shore risk stranding.The findings rested on eyewitness evidence, video footage and expert testimony. The sheriff rejected Greenhowe’s explanations that he was surveying the breakwater on the first date and could not initially see the whales on the second. He concluded that the vessel was driven through a known dolphin foraging area, and straight towards the whales, without regard for the disruption caused. After a trial at Aberdeen Sheriff Court, Greenhowe was convicted on 21 April 2026 and fined £1,000 for the dolphin incident and £1,500 for the pilot whales. Leave to appeal against the sentence was refused, but he was allowed to challenge the convictions on restricted grounds.Why judges ruled that ‘disturb’ has its everyday meaning in Scotland’s marine wildlife lawThe case centred on regulation 39(2) of the Conservation (Natural Habitats, etc) Regulations 1994, which makes it an offence to deliberately or recklessly disturb any dolphin, porpoise or whale. The regulation does not define the word, and the parties could not point to any earlier reported case on it.Greenhowe argued that disturbance of marine mammals is a specialist behavioural issue that a lay observer cannot judge. He relied on guidance from NatureScot, the conservation body formerly known as Scottish Natural Heritage, which describes disturbance as an interaction that changes an animal’s behaviour or environment in a way that affects its well-being or survival in the short, medium or long term. Because a conviction brings a criminal record and a penalty, he said, a low threshold based on a lay impression of momentary distraction was inappropriate and too uncertain.The Crown countered that an undefined word takes its ordinary English meaning, and that accidental disturbance during otherwise lawful marine activity is not criminalised, since the offence requires deliberate or reckless conduct. Sheriff Principal Gillian A Wade KC, delivering the court’s opinion, agreed. She said the guidance could help identify behaviours that might amount to disturbance but could not “trump the primary legislation”. The Shorter Oxford English Dictionary links the word with agitation, intrusion, worry or anxiety, interference with a settled course, frustration and interruption. The court held that the charges gave Greenhowe fair notice that driving over or too close to dolphins and whales was apt to cause exactly that.Why the expert’s cautious wording of ‘likely’ and ‘may’ did not stop the convictionsThe Crown’s skilled witness, Karen Hall of NatureScot, is qualified to assess marine wildlife behaviour. Her report described disturbance of the pilot whales as “likely” and said behavioural changes in the dolphins “may” have been caused by the vessel. Greenhowe argued that such tentative conclusions fell short of proof beyond reasonable doubt, and that eyewitnesses might have seen play or feeding rather than disturbance.The judges said this misunderstood the role of a skilled witness, whose task is to guide a fact-finder through a specialist area, here the behaviour of marine mammals, rather than to settle the issue. The sheriff had to weigh all the evidence, including eyewitness accounts, video footage and Greenhowe’s own explanations, and could accept or reject the expert’s view as with any other witness. The court called the idea that her opinion should displace his own assessment plainly mistaken.It also noted that her evidence did not favour Greenhowe to the extent he suggested. On the pilot whales, Hall’s report found that Seacab clearly breached the Scottish Marine Wildlife Watching Code, described the splitting of the pod as a clear sign of disturbance and called it very fortunate that no stranding occurred. On the dolphins, she noted that the boat came closer than the recommended minimum distance, appeared to speed up and change direction, and was in a key foraging area, all of which raised the risk of disturbance. Breaching, tail slaps, and head slaps, she observed, can also be signs of it.A procedural flaw in the appeal and why the Sheriff Appeal Court still considered the meritsThe stated case contained no questions challenging the sheriff’s findings that the dolphins and pilot whales were disturbed, and the court noted that unless those findings were undone, the appeal had to fail. A question asking whether the sheriff was entitled, on the evidence, to make each finding would have been preferable, the judges said.They nonetheless examined the arguments because the meaning of “disturb” was of some importance, and Greenhowe contended that the sheriff had set the bar for criminal liability too low. His advocate accepted at the hearing that if the word took its dictionary meaning, the remaining questions on expert evidence and the footage would also fall away. articles.title: Mistaken for child-lifter, mentally challenged woman tied up and brutally thrashed by mob in Lucknow
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Hours after a disturbing video showing a woman being tied up and brutally thrashed by a group of people over suspicion of child-lifting went
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Hours after a disturbing video showing a woman being tied up and brutally thrashed by a group of people over suspicion of child-lifting went viral on social media, Lucknow Police arrested three accused in the Indiranagar area on Tuesday.The incident took place near a poultry farm in the Sugamau area. According to police, the woman, a native of Barabanki, is mentally challenged. She had wandered into a nearby settlement of shanties early Tuesday morning and picked up a small child.Suspecting her to be a child-lifter, some residents allegedly caught hold of her, tied her up with a rope and assaulted her with sticks, kicks and punches.The woman's husband, Sandeep Rawat, in his complaint to Indiranagar police, said he and his wife, Lakshmi Rawat, had left home around 5 am when the incident occurred.He alleged that Sunnyuddin, Sariful, Jamaluddin and five to seven unidentified persons attacked his wife, abused her and thrashed her after accusing her of attempting to kidnap a child.Rawat said he initially took his injured wife to Balrampur Hospital, where she was provided treatment and discharged. However, when she subsequently complained of abdominal pain, he admitted her to RML Hospital for further treatment.He said he later came across a video of the assault showing several people thrashing his wife, following which he approached the police and lodged a written complaint.Taking cognisance of the viral video, Indiranagar police initiated an inquiry and subsequently registered an FIR based on the husband's complaint.Three accused have been arrested, while efforts are underway to identify and apprehend the remaining persons involved in the assault.Additional DCP, East Zone, Amol Murkut, told TOI that Sunnyudul, Mohammed Annuddin and Jamaluddin had been arrested. articles.title: New regulation for heating oil market, but no price controls
articles.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority has investigated the heating oil market in Northern Ireland and other parts of the UK.
articles.body:
Home heating oil suppliers in Northern Ireland will face stricter regulation in the wake of an inquiry by the UK's competition watchdog.

However it will not include the sort of price controls applied to the gas and electricity markets.

The Economy Minister Caoimhe Archibald said she will now act on the CMA's recommendations.

"The CMA identified the need for stronger consumer protection, support for vulnerable households, and more formal dispute resolution arrangements," she told MLAs.

She said the changes she was announcing are "proportionate" and will enhance existing heating oil consumer protection "at minimal additional cost".

What regulations will be put in place for home heating oil?

The measures include a mandatory code of conduct for heating oil suppliers and giving the Consumer Council an enhanced role in helping consumers resolve disputes.

The Consumer Council will also lead in the creation of an opt-in register for vulnerable consumers.

About two thirds of Northern Ireland households use home heating oil, by far the highest of any UK region.

At the start of the US-Israel attack on Iran in March, heating oil prices in Northern Ireland rose by a record monthly rate of 92% .

That compared to the previous largest spike of 59% in March 2022, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Analysis by the CMA suggested that prices rose even more steeply in Scotland and Wales, where heating oil is typically used in remote rural areas.

It found that prices tended to be lower in Northern Ireland overall as it has a competitive range of suppliers and a market which is big enough to minimise delivery costs.

The CMA said that the huge spike in prices at the start of the Iran conflict largely reflected rising wholesale costs.

It did not recommend price controls suggesting they could be counterproductive.

articles.body: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has defended the decision to launch military action against Iran, saying he would support the operation again despite concerns about its political consequences and its possible role in Republican losses in the midterm elections.During a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth was asked whether he agreed with Vice President JD Vance's assessment that the Iran war was a major reason Republicans lost ground in the midterms.Hegseth said he had great respect for Vance but would not assign blame for the election outcome.“I respect JD greatly, and I’m certainly not going to engage in any finger-pointing,” he said.Hegseth said his focus was on the Pentagon's responsibilities rather than electoral politics. “Thankfully, politics is not really my thing. I do the Department of War and make sure we’re prepared and ready,” he said, adding that others would assess the conflict and its consequences.However, he backed President Donald Trump's position that the military action was justified and said he would support the decision again, even if it remained unpopular with the public.“Absolutely. It was done for the right reasons to ensure Iran never gets a nuclear weapon,” Hegseth said.He also endorsed Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assessment that the operation may have been necessary despite lacking public support. “It’s not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary, and that’s certainly how I feel,” Hegseth said.The US administration has given several explanations for the decision to attack Iran. The White House had said in June 2025 that US strikes had “obliterated” Iran's nuclear programme.Hegseth also declined to comment directly on reports that White House chief of staff Stephen Miller believes the war should end. articles.title: 2008 CRPF camp attack convict shot dead by unknown gunman in UP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An unknown gunman shot dead Mohammad Sharif, an accused linked to the 2008 CRPF camp attack, on Tuesday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An unknown gunman shot dead Mohammad Sharif, an accused linked to the 2008 CRPF camp attack, on Tuesday. Sharif was killed in Rampur, UP with bystanders alleging he was shot 16 times. The police have initiated a manhunt for the shooter/s.Seven CRPF personnel and a rickshaw puller were killed in a pre-dawn terror attack, plotted by Lashkar-e-Taiba, on the CRPF Group Centre in Rampur on the night of December 31, 2007-Jan 1, 2008. In May 2025, unknown gunmen had killed Abu Saifullah Khalid, a key Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) operative and the mastermind behind the 2006 RSS headquarters attack and multiple terror strikes, including one on a CRPF camp in Uttar Pradesh.Sharif, who belonged to Badanpuri-Khajuria village in Rampur, went by aliases of Suhail, Sajid, Anwar and Ali, according to police records. He was lodged in Bareilly central jail and released last Nov.Arrested in the case in the aftermath of the attack, a UP court had in 2019 convicted Sharif and five others including two Pakistani nationals in the case. Four including Sharif were subsequently sentenced to death after they were found directly involved in the attack.In Oct 2025, the Allahabad High Court, however, overturned the death sentences but upheld their conviction under the Arms Act for possessing prohibited weapons, sentencing them to ten years’ rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 lakh each. The HC had noted procedural lapses by the police like failure to conduct a Test Identification Parade (TIP) and also found lapses in the handling of physical evidence, observing that firearms, cartridges, and grenades allegedly recovered from the scene were not securely preserved or properly traced through the chain of custody. articles.title: Chappelle, Jennifer Welch jokes about Kirk's murder part of pattern of leftists finding humor in violence
articles.summary: From Dave Chappelle's Charlie Kirk joke to several Trump assassination quips, a growing list of liberal figures have promoted political violence.
articles.body: Charlie Kirk, the conservative icon and Turning Point USA co-founder who was assassinated in 2025, has been the subject of viral jokes, particularly following last week's midterm elections, which saw Democrats score victories over Republicans. "I've Had It" co-hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan went viral after celebrating Democratic victories and laughing uncontrollably last week at an online post that read, "We're digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again." Several of the podcast's sponsors pulled their support following pressure from Kirk's supporters, prompting Welch and Sullivan to issue a statement apologizing for their conduct and advocating for gun control. Welch later doubled down in a separate video posted Sunday. "When we apologize for laughing at a joke on our podcast, that wasn't for you. That was for us," Welch said in response to comments made by Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet, saying it was for someone she knew personally who was killed in an act of gun violence. On Saturday, the two hosts apologized on Instagram. "On Thursday’s show, we laughed at a joke about Charlie Kirk. It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize," the statement read. "Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence." WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN Meanwhile, a video circulated of comedian Dave Chappelle performing over the weekend at Madison Square Garden, in which he told the crowd, "I feel better," while discussing Kirk's assassination. Notably, Kirk had previously condemned the "armed maniac" who attacked Chappelle onstage in 2022 and called for harsher criminal charges against the attacker. Chappelle and Welch are among several entertainers and commentators who have joked about political violence targeting conservatives or made remarks interpreted as encouraging such violence in recent years. CHARLAMAGNE THA GOD CALLS OUT DAVE CHAPPELLE'S KIRK COMMENTS, WOULDN'T WISH THEM 'ON MY WORST ENEMY' Jokes about assassinating Trump The promoting of President Donald Trump's assassination began within hours of him being sworn into office in 2017. At a Woman's March rally held the day after his inauguration in Washington, D.C., music superstar Madonna told the crowd, "I have thought an awful lot about blowing up the White House." In May 2017, liberal comedian Kathy Griffin sparked a national controversy when she posed for a photo shoot holding a prop of Trump's bloodied severed head. That June, actor Johnny Depp alluded to President Abraham Lincoln's assassination while discussing Trump, saying "When was the last time an actor assassinated a president? I want to clarify: I’m not an actor. I lie for a living. However, it’s been a while, and maybe it’s time." 10 CELEBRITIES WHO HAVE JOKED ABOUT TRUMP'S DEATH, FROM KATHY GRIFFIN TO JIMMY KIMMEL The jokes about Trump continued even after the assassination attempts against him in 2024. Hours after the Butler shooting that July, Kyle Gass of the band Tenacious D made a birthday wish while blowing out candles at a concert, saying, "Don't miss Trump next time." In April 2026, "Saturday Night Live" cast member Michael Che set up a joke by noting that Trump had attended the opening night performance of "Chicago" at the Kennedy Center during "Weekend Update." "I think that's cool that the president is going to the theater. I mean — what's the worst that could happen?" Che said with a grin, referencing Lincoln's assassination. Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel also drew controversy earlier this year for joking that First Lady Melania Trump had "the glow of an expectant widow" days before the assassination attempt at the White House Correspondents Dinner. Kimmel later insisted the joke was referring to the age gap between her and her husband. Others who've joked about killing Trump include George Lopez and the late Broadway actress Carole Cook. BILL MAHER TORCHES FAR-LEFT ASSASSINATION CULTURE AFTER STRING OF HIGH-PROFILE ATTACKS Violent rhetoric towards GOP lawmakers It's not just Trump and Kirk who have been the subject of violent rhetoric. Republican lawmakers have faced similar ire from prominent leftists. Some public figures have mocked Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., who was assaulted by his neighbor in 2017 following a dispute over yard maintenance. Paul suffered six broken ribs and later underwent surgery. Actress Bette Midler made multiple jokes at Paul's expense, writing in 2018, "Where’s Rand Paul’s neighbor when we need him?" as he debated a federal spending bill. In 2019, in response to Paul's comments about Kurdish fighters in Syria, Midler said, "I DO NOT promote violence but...Rand Paul says the Kurds are being 'ingrates' for taking their frustrations out on U.S. Troops. Which is a good reminder for us all to be more grateful for the neighbor who beat the s--- out of Rand Paul." Midler also made a remark about stabbing Trump, writing in another post, "Maybe someone in his camp can gently give him a shiv. I mean, shove." In 2025, progressive commentator Hasan Piker told his audience, "If you cared about Medicare fraud, or Medicaid fraud, you would kill Rick Scott," pointing to the senator's past tenure at a healthcare company that pleaded guilty to fraud. Piker later walked back the comment, suggesting Scott should face "MAX PUNISHMENT" instead. Piker also called for the murder of landlords and property owners in a separate livestream. "Kill them! KiII those motherf—-ers and murder those motherf—-ers in the streets... Let the streets soak in their f—ing red capitalist blood," Piker said. The 'execution' of Elon Musk Earlier this month, New York University professor and podcast host Scott Galloway called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk a "traitor" and suggested he should face the same punishment as Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, after reports emerged about Musk's alleged involvement in restricting Starlink satellite internet speeds in Ukraine. The Rosenbergs were executed in 1953 after being convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage on behalf of the Soviet Union. "We lined up the Rosenbergs against a wall. This is a traitor to the West, and he should be held to the same standards as every other traitor in the West," Galloway said. Turning Point, the group leading the cancellation against us, mocks violence and never apologizes," Welch told Fox News Digital. "We still have plenty of advertisers and we aren't going anywhere," she continued. "Each and every day we will relentlessly fight for equality and justice for every American, and we enthusiastically welcome the nearly 30,000 new followers that have come to our channel in the last few days." articles.title: Months after the deaths of Rob and Michele Reiner, a Los Angeles children’s charity raised a record $4 million at a gala honouring their legacy; their children presented an award to Jamie Lee Curtis
articles.summary: Months after the deaths of Rob and Michele Reiner, the Children’s Institute turned its annual Cape & Gown Gala into a record-setting tribute to their work
articles.body: Months after the deaths of Rob and Michele Reiner, the Children’s Institute turned its annual Cape & Gown Gala into a record-setting tribute to their work on behalf of children and families. The Los Angeles charity raised $4 million at the November 8 event, according to a PR Newswire release, drawing more than 600 guests to the Beverly Wilshire Hotel in Beverly Hills.The evening honored the Reiners’ decades of advocacy, including their role in creating First 5 California and their support for the legal challenge that helped pave the way for marriage equality nationwide. Their children, Jake and Romy Reiner, presented the inaugural Michele & Rob Reiner Champion for Change Award to Jamie Lee Curtis.A record-setting nightThe $4 million raised at the gala marks a record for Children’s Institute, according to the organization. The funds will support programs that help children and families heal from trauma, succeed in school and build pathways toward long-term health, stability and economic mobility.More than 600 guests attended the event, which was held as Children’s Institute celebrates its 120th anniversary. Founded in 1906, the organization provides early childhood education, mental health services and whole-family support to roughly 30,000 children and families across Los Angeles County each year.The gala was not simply a fundraising event. It became a gathering point for friends, collaborators and advocates who wanted to celebrate the values the Reiners represented, including compassion, urgency and a willingness to challenge systems that fail children.Children’s Institute President and CEO Martine Singer described Rob and Michele as “a force field,” saying their love was generous, fierce and unconditional. She said the organization’s mission is to continue expressing that sense of urgency and to use its own voice to amplify the power of their work.A tribute from their childrenJake and Romy Reiner presented the inaugural Champion for Change Award to Jamie Lee Curtis, a choice that reflected both their parents’ values and Curtis’s long history of advocacy for children and families. The award was created in partnership with their aunt, Martine Singer, as a lasting tribute to the Reiners’ contributions to American civic life.Jake Reiner said the name of the award captured what his parents stood for. He described them as people who were never satisfied with the status quo and who consistently worked to make the world better, beginning with the loving environment they created at home.Romy Reiner spoke about Curtis’s generosity during a difficult period for the family. She said Curtis believes in the good in people and will do everything she can to make a situation right, adding that her support has meant more than she can fully express.For Curtis, the award carried personal meaning. She said Rob and Michele “lived so fiercely, so loudly,” and described them as undeniable. Her remarks framed the evening as a celebration of people who refused to remain silent in the face of injustice or need.Jamie Lee Curtis honoredCurtis received the inaugural Michele & Rob Reiner Champion for Change Award in recognition of her longstanding commitment to children and families. Her charitable initiative, My Hand In Yours, has raised nearly $2 million for Children’s Hospital Los Angeles.She is also the author of 14 children’s books, including Just One More Sleep, published in 2024. That body of work made her a natural fit for an award created to honor people who combine public influence with direct service to young people.Curtis’s connection to the Reiners goes beyond shared values. Her presence at the gala added emotional weight to an evening already shaped by grief, remembrance and a shared commitment to improving the lives of children.The award also gave the Reiner children a way to turn loss into action. Rather than allowing the evening to become only a memorial, they used it to recognize someone whose work reflects the same spirit of service their parents embodied.A night of music and memoryJohn Mayer performed at the gala, singing “The Heart of Life” and “Gravity.” His connection to Rob Reiner added another layer of meaning to the evening, since Mayer’s song “Say,” featured in Reiner’s 2007 film The Bucket List, earned him the 2009 Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance.Comedian, television host and author Chelsea Handler also appeared, bringing humor to an emotional night. She told guests that Rob and Michele had brought so many people together and that the community could continue celebrating their values through the work of Children’s Institute.Emmy-winning filmmaker Barry Sonnenfeld served as emcee. His friendship and creative partnership with Rob Reiner spanned decades, including work on When Harry Met Sally and Misery, and he was also the person who introduced Rob to Michele Singer.Sonnenfeld described the couple as extraordinary, powerful and deeply caring. His remarks reflected the sense among those who knew them that the Reiners’ influence was not limited to film or politics, but extended into the personal lives of the people around them.A legacy that continuesRob and Michele Reiner’s work had a lasting impact on public policy and social causes. Their leadership helped establish First 5 California, which generated billions of dollars in funding and created a lasting investment in early childhood programs.They also played a pivotal role in the federal court challenge to California’s ban on marriage equality, an effort that helped set the stage for marriage equality nationwide. Those accomplishments explain why Children’s Institute chose to honor them not only as philanthropists, but as advocates who changed the terms of public debate.The $4 million raised at the gala ensures that their legacy will continue in a practical way. The funds will support services for children and families across Los Angeles County, extending the Reiners’ commitment to early childhood, mental health and family stability.For the Reiner children, the evening was a chance to honor their parents in the most meaningful way possible, by continuing the work they believed in. For Children’s Institute, it was a reminder that a legacy is not measured only by what someone builds, but by what continues after they are gone.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Deadly Egypt train crash prompts calls for political accountability
articles.summary: A deadly train collision in Egypt’s al-Ayyat prompts demands for political accountability and rail upgrade reviews.
articles.body:
A deadly train collision in the outskirts of the Egyptian capital Cairo , which killed at least seven people and injured more than 125 others according to the country’s Ministry of Health and Population, has ignited a wave of parliamentary and political demands for accountability. The disaster raises urgent questions about the effect of the millions of dollars the Egyptian state has poured into upgrading the railway network and whether those investments are genuinely improving passenger safety.

A train travelling between Giza and Fayoum on Sunday ran into the back of another train on the Cairo-to-Aswan route, causing the latter to derail onto a countryside road in al-Ayyat district. Following the crash, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

The Egyptian parliament’s Transport and Communications Committee summoned Transport Minister Kamel el-Wazir to an emergency session on Tuesday to investigate. Meanwhile, opposition voices have escalated demands for political accountability, ranging from criticising the minister to demanding the dismissal of the entire government.

Abdel Moneim Imam, a member of Parliament and head of the Justice Party, told Al Jazeera that the situation requires decisive action, and highlighted several previous train disasters in al-Ayyat. A 2002 fire killed more than 370 people, while a train collision in 2009 killed 15 people, and three separate collisions in 2016 killed 14 people in total.

Al-Ayyat is a major corridor for trains travelling between Cairo and southern Egypt, with heavy railway traffic and railway switches in the area.

“The recurrence of train accidents in the al-Ayyat area, despite what the Transport Ministry has repeatedly announced regarding the development of the railway system, reflects the absence of genuine accountability for the officials responsible for those accidents,” Imam stated.

“Taking decisive measures and holding officials accountable for previous accidents would have prevented the recurrence of these scenes,” he added. “The minister of transport enjoys the protection of the parliamentary majority, which prevents the activation of parliamentary accountability … The continued turning of a blind eye to the shortcomings and the recurrence of accidents without genuine accountability leads to the continuation of the crisis.”

Imam, who has described himself as a reformist politician, called for ministers to be questioned in Parliament over the latest accident.

Egypt’s parliamentary transport committee met on Tuesday in the presence of Transport Minister Kamal el-Wazir to discuss the circumstances of Sunday’s train collision, and measures to prevent similar accidents.

However, Ahmed el-Derby, the secretary of the committee, told Al Jazeera before the meeting that its purpose was not to “interrogate [el-Wazir] or confront him with premeditated accusations”.

Asked whether the government bore political responsibility for railway accidents, el-Derby said that ultimate responsibility rested with those overseeing the railway system.

“Officials bear responsibility for mistakes that occur during their tenure, even if they did not personally make those mistakes,” el-Derby said, adding that the accident showed that something had gone wrong and that an investigation was needed to establish who was responsible and hold them accountable.

“We do not support the hasty demands to dismiss officials, and dismissals alone do not represent a solution to the crisis,” he said.

Atef el-Maghawry, head of the Tagammu Party’s parliamentary bloc, said the repeated railways accidents in al-Ayyat pointed to wider government failures, rather than problems confined to the Transport Ministry.

“Despite the ministrys announcements about upgrading the railway network and signalling systems, the recurrence of accidents in al-Ayyat points to a crisis that goes beyond the the Transport Ministry and reflects broader government policies,” he told Al Jazeera.

El-Maghrawy argued that replacing the transport minister would not be enough, and instead called for the dismissal of the entire government over its failures to address a wide range of social issues.

“What is required is a change in policies, not simply a change of personnel,” he said.

“There are achievements that have been realised in the railway sector, and other sectors, but questions remain regarding the cost of these achievements and the results entailed by them,” el-Maghawry explained.

Parliamentarians are now demanding answers on railway funding. Irene Saeed, head of the Reform and Development Party’s parliamentary bloc, called for a detailed breakdown of how the Transport Ministry spent loans obtained in 2026.

Saeed wants to know what proportion of loans taken out by the ministry during el-Wazir’s tenure went towards safety, signalling and maintenance, and how many accidents in 2025 and 2026 were found to be the railway authority’s responsibility.

The Transport Ministry says approximately $37bn was allocated to transport investments between 2014 and 2024.

Hassan Mahdy, a highway engineering professor at Ain Shams University, warned against drawing conclusions before the investigation is complete. He pointed to upgrades across Egypt’s railway network, including a shift to electronic systems intended to manage train movements and reduce reliance on human intervention.

Mahdy said that investigators had to establish why one of the trains stopped on the main track – highlighting the possibility of a sudden technical failure or someone activating the emergency brake. In addition, investigators would need to verify whether the second train’s signalling system warned its driver of a stationary train on the line before the collision.

El-Derby said that the railway signals had issued a stop instruction, citing information from the signalling director, but it remained unclear whether the driver received the warning early enough to stop.

He also urged caution about directly comparing the collison with the previous deadly incidents in al-Ayyat, saying railway operations and signalling have since been upgraded.

“The results of the investigations will reveal all the circumstances of the accident, whether the cause is linked to the human element or a technical flaw in the system,” Mahdy said.

articles.title: CPCB explains why official AQI is capped at 500 despite private apps showing higher readings
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Central Pollution Control Board on Tuesday defended its air quality monitoring methodology, explaining why official AQI readings are capped
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Central Pollution Control Board on Tuesday defended its air quality monitoring methodology, explaining why official AQI readings are capped at 500 even as private monitoring apps reported levels as high as 1,800 in Delhi after Diwali.The clarification came amid questions over the wide disparity between government data and readings displayed by private air quality monitoring platforms.The CPCB said the 500-point ceiling was an intentional feature of the National Air Quality Index (NAQI), consistent with international practices. It explained that readings beyond 500 would not change the health advisory, as all such levels fall under the 'Severe' category."The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a tool for effective communication of air quality status to the people in terms that are easy to understand. AQI is an indicative scale designed to convey the likely health implications of prevailing air quality conditions. The AQI category along with the associated health statement is more significant than the corresponding AQI value within that category," the board said in a statement.The CPCB said the official index uses scientifically validated 24-hour rolling averages to assess sustained exposure to pollutants. Private apps, on the other hand, often capture hourly fluctuations through low-cost sensors, which may show sharp spikes in pollution levels.According to the board, the NAQI has six categories - 'Good', 'Satisfactory', 'Moderately Polluted', 'Poor', 'Very Poor' and 'Severe' - within a scale of 0 to 500. It said an AQI reading of 500 or above indicates broadly similar health risks and therefore does not warrant a separate category."Beyond this level the AQI remains in the 'Severe' category and extrapolation of the index would not alter the assigned health impact category. The capping at 500 is thus a design feature of the index, as has been evolved in 2015 methodology of NAQI in line with the prevailing international practice including US EPA AQI scale," it added.CPCB also said private apps could report higher readings during brief pollution spikes but show lower figures when pollution levels subsequently decline."It is generally perceived that private apps show higher AQI. This may hold during short peaks, when hourly values rise sharply. However, when concentrations fall, such apps show lower AQI than the NAQI, since the NAQI continues to reflect the exposure of the preceding 24 hours," it said."This has also been evident in Delhi post Diwali firecrackers bursting event. The NAQI thus provides a consistent and reliable indication of the likely health impacts of sustained exposure to pollutants, which is the scientifically relevant measure for public health advisories," it further said.The clarification came as social media posts showing screenshots of private air quality apps reporting AQI levels between 1,500 and 1,800 in Delhi on Diwali night, while CPCB's official readings remained below 400.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Riot-torn France struggles with chaos at home as Macron eyes military mission thousands of miles away
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron's Lebanon military force plan hits resistance from Italy as Marco Rubio floats a civilian alternative to UNIFIL.
articles.body: French President Emmanuel Macron is pushing ahead with plans for a new European military presence in Lebanon while struggling with mounting political and economic turmoil at home, even as the initiative encounters resistance from a key European partner and Washington considers an alternative that may not require troops. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that he had discussed the future of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) with Macron, suggesting that a replacement monitoring mechanism could be civilian rather than military. "It doesn't have to be a military mission. It could be a civilian mission," Rubio said in remarks published Tuesday. Rubio explained that the administration is seeking a credible mechanism to verify arrangements under which Israeli forces withdraw from designated areas, the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) assume control and the Iran-backed terrorist group Hezbollah is prevented from returning. RUBIO ANNOUNCES FRAMEWORK DEAL BETWEEN ISRAEL AND LEBANON AS EXPERTS WARN IRAN WILL FIGHT TO SABOTAGE IT He suggested France could play a constructive role but emphasized that any arrangement would require agreement from both Lebanon and Israel. U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz also made clear that Washington has no intention of preserving the existing peacekeeping mission. "UNIFIL in its current form will not continue, and it must not continue — we are working with our international partners to draw down the mission and ensure that the Lebanese people can choose their own future and to ensure that the Lebanese Armed Forces can secure the nation’s future," Waltz told Fox News Digital. MACRON UNDER FIRE OVER IRAN, HEZBOLLAH POLICY AS TRUMP ADMIN HOSTS ISRAEL-LEBANON TALKS The French initiative, meanwhile, envisions a multinational force potentially involving thousands of European troops to support the Lebanese army as UNIFIL prepares to end its nearly five-decade mission. The proposed force's final size, mandate and participating countries remain unconfirmed. However, Italy, which previously joined France in calling for an international coalition following UNIFIL's withdrawal, does not support deploying its troops under the proposal currently advanced by Paris, three sources with knowledge of the discussions told Fox News Digital. The initiative comes as Macron faces growing domestic pressure, with France experiencing widespread demonstrations over rising living costs, wages and deteriorating public services. The unrest has further complicated the government's efforts to pass its 2027 budget, as mounting debt and political divisions limit its room to maneuver, Reuters reported Nov. 5. Against that backdrop, France's proposed deployment raises questions about the financial and military resources Paris could commit to another overseas mission, particularly without firm support from its European partners. Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, senior envoy for Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, argued that replacing UNIFIL with another international military force risks repeating the shortcomings of the existing mission. "UNIFIL’s mandate should end as scheduled. Hezbollah built up its military presence in southern Lebanon with international peacekeepers already on the ground. Keeping troops there under a new mandate would repeat an approach that failed to prevent that buildup. The basis for what comes next should be the U.S.-brokered agreement Israel and Lebanon reached in June. France can help both sides put it into practice and move further," Rodan-Benzaquen told Fox News Digital. FRANCE IS DEVOURING ITSELF AS SCHOOL RIOTS REVEAL A CRISIS FAR BIGGER THAN BROKEN CLASSROOMS The question of who would conduct such inspections has already proved contentious. The United States and Israel had previously opposed France serving as a third-party verifier of Hezbollah's disarmament, according to an Aug. 7 Reuters report citing Lebanese officials and foreign diplomats. A Lebanese official also told Reuters that Beirut had rejected an earlier proposal involving private security companies. The challenges extend beyond diplomatic disagreements. According to a Congressional Research Service assessment updated November 9, Hezbollah continues to refuse disarmament while Israeli forces maintain positions in southern Lebanon. IS THE IRAN-BACKED TERRORIST MOVEMENT HEZBOLLAH ON THE ROPES IN LEBANON? A U.S.-brokered framework agreement reached in June linked a phased Israeli withdrawal to the verified disarmament of armed groups and the deployment of Lebanese forces. But implementation has stalled beyond the initial pilot areas, and negotiations in October ended without agreement. Rather than committing additional troops, Rodan-Benzaquen argued that Paris should focus on using its diplomatic influence to strengthen the Lebanese government's efforts to disarm Hezbollah. "France’s greatest leverage is notably in Beirut. The Lebanese cabinet has already outlawed Hezbollah’s military activity. Paris should work with the Lebanese government to press disarming Hezbollah. Israel needs credible evidence that Hezbollah cannot return to an area its troops are eventually leaving. Beirut needs confidence that once its army secures that area, the agreed Israeli withdrawal will eventually follow. That is where French diplomacy can make a difference." The debate follows the August 2025 Security Council resolution extending UNIFIL's mandate for a final time, until December 31, 2026, with an orderly withdrawal authorized over the following year. Washington backed terminating the mission amid longstanding concerns about its inability to prevent Hezbollah from maintaining a military presence in southern Lebanon. France, by contrast, has warned against leaving a security vacuum. PENTAGON HOSTS FIRST-EVER ISRAELI–LEBANESE MILITARY TALKS AIMED AT CURBING HEZBOLLAH In a previous Security Council statement, the French Mission to the U.N. said: "France will support UNIFIL until the expiration of its mandate. It will contribute to defining the future international engagement in Lebanon, in support of its sovereignty and the implementation of resolution 1701." U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric told Fox News Digital that Secretary-General António Guterres presented three options for a future U.N. presence in June, but the Security Council has not formally selected one. He added that the U.N. is aware of discussions about a possible non-U.N. military presence in southern Lebanon but is not directly involved in those negotiations. With UNIFIL's mandate approaching expiration, France faces the challenge of securing agreement not only on which countries would contribute personnel, but also on what those forces would be authorized to do in a country where Hezbollah remains armed and Israeli troops have yet to fully withdraw. Requests for comment were also sent to the State Department, Spanish and Lebanese authorities.

articles.title: Charity calls for stronger protections for Guernsey trees
articles.summary: Guernsey Trees for Life believes trees over a certain size should be protected by default.
articles.body:
A charity is calling for more protections for trees.

Guernsey Trees for Life has written a letter to deputies, seeking stronger legal protection for trees and the environment; with Colin Dodd, from the charity, saying the island was losing "a lot of trees" to development.

He said: "We've had about four or five cases this year of that sort of thing happening. If there's a 200-year-old oak tree on-site, it's very easy just to put a bulldozer in there. All we're saying is we need some sort of blanket protection for trees."

The charity said tree protection orders tended to be "reactive" not "proactive", applying to trees once they were under threat. The BBC has approached the States of Guernsey.

He added: "We all need development but it needs to be in harmony with our environment.

"It's very easy to give that site a little more thought, jig things around slightly and include that tree or that part of the natural environment within that development."

In a letter to deputies, the charity said tree protection orders were "purely reactive".

It said the process was "slow and complex and does not automatically protect trees within new planning schemes".

The letter said trees were only protected after threat, leaving them "unprotected against sudden felling or development."

The charity said it believed trees over a certain size should be protected by default.

"We could exempt certain species of course," Dodd said.

"All we're saying is we need some sort of blanket protection for trees."

articles.title: Meghan Markle made her first public appearance since her father's arrest, but withdrew from a planned speech at the European Parliament as Prince Harry opened a memorial for children harmed online in Brussels
articles.summary: Meghan Markle made her first public appearance alongside Prince Harry in Brussels on Tuesday.
articles.body: Meghan Markle made her first public appearance alongside Prince Harry in Brussels on Tuesday. She joined her husband at the European Parliament just days after reports emerged that her estranged father had been arrested in the United States. Although the Duchess of Sussex accompanied Harry to the European venue, she decided not to take part in their planned joint speech and panel discussion. Prince Harry delivered the address on his own at an event that opened a memorial for children who have lost their lives because of online harm, according to Reuters and Agence France-Presse (AFP). The visit to Belgium was the couple's first public appearance since Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested in Florida on federal charges linked to the possession of child sexual abuse material. He has denied the allegation. According to a report by Turkish news agency Anadolu Agency, the Duchess stepped away from her planned speaking role because she did not feel emotionally ready to speak publicly following the news about her father.European Parliament memorial openingThe royal couple travelled to Brussels to attend an event at the European Parliament focused on online safety and protecting children. Details of the gathering were reported by Politico Europe and international news outlets, including the Associated Press. The event marked the opening of a memorial for children who have died or suffered harm because of online exploitation, cyberbullying, and dangerous content on digital platforms. Harry and Meghan were both originally expected to speak at the event. However, the Duchess chose to attend without giving a speech. Harry went ahead with the opening address and took part in a panel discussion with international safety campaigners and European lawmakers. The group included members of the Internal Market Committee, which is working on the EU's Kids Act. During his speech, Harry spoke about the growing dangers children face on digital platforms. He also called on technology companies to take greater responsibility for keeping their users safe.Call for technology firm accountabilitySpeaking to European lawmakers and campaigners, the Duke of Sussex strongly criticised major online platforms. He accused technology companies of creating an online environment filled with division and irresponsible behaviour. "Major technology companies are creating a world of chaos, division and irresponsibility," Harry said during his speech at the European Parliament, according to Politico Europe. He called for stronger rules and closer government oversight to protect young users from harmful content that could lead to self-harm or suicide. Harry also raised concerns about the privacy policies used by technology companies. He argued that unclear rules often make it difficult for grieving parents to understand what happened to their children online. The Duke said digital platforms must be more open about their policies and work closely with regulators. He stressed that these changes are needed to prevent further tragedies involving children.Personal turmoil surrounding family allegationsThe couple's visit to Brussels took place during a difficult period for the family following the legal action involving Meghan's estranged father in Florida. After Thomas Markle Sr.'s arrest, the Duchess released a statement saying she was "deeply distressed" by the allegations, according to reports by AFP and RTL Today. Meghan also said she had previously ended contact between her father and her two children, Archie and Lilibet, because of earlier troubling behaviour. Despite the personal difficulties, Meghan chose to travel to Belgium with Harry to support the online safety campaign. However, she decided to step back from her planned speaking role at the event. The couple's appearance at the European Parliament marks their latest international visit focused on protecting children online. articles.title: ITV Wales plans to cut programmes and jobs
articles.summary: Coast and Country and Backstage face the axe, while ITV Wales plans to cut producer roles.
articles.body:
ITV Wales plans to cut two programmes and reduce the number of producer roles in its Cardiff headquarters.

The broadcaster said the proposals would "help to ease some cost pressure" and would allow its English language teams to "work more flexibly".

ITV confirmed it was proposing to end its long-running Coast and Country show and weekly arts and entertainment programme Backstage.

The changes would not affect the amount of news and current affairs programmes which are broadcast by ITV Wales each week.

A spokesperson said the broadcaster had begun consulting with staff after informing most of them about the proposals on Tuesday morning.

Coast and Country has run for over a decade and focuses on rural communities, the environment and the Welsh countryside.

It has been presented by weather presenter Ruth Dodsworth and Sean Fletcher.

BBC Wales understands that the number of producers working at ITV Wales may reduce from six to two as part of the restructure, while efforts to reduce expenditure could mean more programmes are made in the studio rather than on location.

An ITV Cymru Wales spokesperson said the wider industry was under "significant economic pressure" and these proposals were part of efforts to mitigate some of that financial strain.

They added that its plan to "restructure some of the teams that make our English language programmes to enable us to work more flexibly" while protecting its commitments to audience and the regulator, Ofcom.

Earlier this year, Sky agreed a £1.6bn deal to buy ITV's broadcasting and streaming operations, while leaving ITV Studios as a separate company. The takeover is subject to scrutiny , and may not proceed until late 2027.

In September BBC Wales announced it would cut 58 jobs as part of wider efforts across the BBC to save £500 million.

articles.summary: Wayne Siegler pleaded guilty to possessing cocaine and will appear at a second hearing in December.
articles.body:
An American pilot has admitted possessing cocaine after being arrested at Heathrow Airport earlier this month.

Wayne Sigler, 64, from Louisiana, was detained by police on Sunday 1 November and appeared at Uxbridge Magistrates Court on Saturday. After pleading guilty to the possession offence he was placed into custody, the Metropolitan Police confirmed.

He has also been charged with being drunk or unfit to fly while flying or working on an aircraft - two offences that fall under the Railway and Transport Act 2003.

He is due appear for his next hearing at Isleworth Crown Court on 7 December.

Police have not specified which company the pilot was working for when he was arrested.

Heathrow Airport has declined to comment.

articles.title: Israeli president warns against repeat election in new Knesset session
articles.summary: Herzog calls for an inquiry into the October 7 attacks during a Knesset session amid political gridlock following elections.
articles.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged lawmakers to “leave no stone unturned” and launch an investigation into the October 7 attacks by Hamas in a speech opening the new parliamentary session, after the election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc short of a majority.

Herzog called on party leaders to “make concessions” and do “everything possible to avoid a repeat election” at the swearing-in of newly elected members in the 26th Knesset on Tuesday.

The Israeli president tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government on Sunday, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

While also short of a parliamentary majority, Eisenkot and his allies hope to use their newfound legislative power to move rapidly to establish an independent inquiry into the October 7 attacks.

“I am committed in this complex situation to form a national emergency government as quickly as possible,” Eisenkot said, ahead of the Knesset session.

Netanyahu has previously refused to form a commission to investigate the attacks, arguing that a panel appointed by the Israeli Supreme Court would be biased against the government.

On Iran, Herzog said in his speech that Tehran “does not stop even for a moment in its plots and threats, whether directly or through its partners”, repeating the notion from his speech officially delegating Eisenkot to form the new government.

The president said Israel “must fortify the alliance” with the United States amid increasing disapproval of Israel among the US public due to the genocidal war on Gaza and the US-Israel war on Iran.

“Alongside the stubborn and determined war against those who seek to harm us, we must build a stable political horizon in the region with our neighbours,” he said, adding that Israel must “strengthen and even add to the peace agreements with Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, the United Arab Emirates, and Bahrain”.

The speaker of the Knesset, a member of Netanyahu’s Likud Party, will remain in the caretaker position until a new vote is held.

“Yashar, Eisenkot’s party, has already submitted 61 signatures of new parliamentarians demanding that the vote take place as soon as possible,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from the occupied West Bank.

Netanyahu and his bloc continue to protest the result of the October 27 elections, claiming foreign interference after Palestinian-Israeli parties secured a 19-seat bloc.

“Those protests have gone unanswered because the results have been certified and every relevant authority has dismissed the allegations that there were widespread violations,” Odeh said.

Eisenkot has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government. If neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu forms a coalition, another round of elections could follow.

articles.title: ​A Washington woman says her ex-husband tracked her spending, accessed her home’s Alexa system and repeatedly stalked her despite a no-contact order; an appeals court upheld a five-year domestic violence protection order
articles.summary: A Washington woman sought a domestic violence protection order after her ex-husband allegedly tracked her spending and even accessed her home’s Alexa
articles.body: A Washington woman sought a domestic violence protection order after her ex-husband allegedly tracked her spending and even accessed her home’s Alexa device, despite a court-issued no-contact order. The Washington Court of Appeals upheld a five-year protection order, rejecting his challenge, in the ruling issued on Monday, Nov. 9.A night that ended in an arrestThe couple married in 2006. They have one adult son, who was still a minor when the events that led to this case began. In December 2020, the couple argued. The husband became angry, followed his wife up the stairs, pushed her into a room, strangled her and twisted her head, according to court records. When she tried to get their son to call 911, he lifted her off the floor and covered her mouth. Police arrested him. He later pleaded guilty to fourth-degree assault.After the incident, the husband moved out and filed for divorce. In September 2021, a criminal court ordered him to stay away from his wife, her home, her workplace and any place she was. However, he had other plans. He kept contacting her anyway, the records show. A month later, he came to the family home while his wife was out of town. He knew she was away because he had been tracking her credit card purchases. The following month, he used an Alexa device inside the house to ‘drop in’ on the household. That same month, he accessed his wife’s email account and changed her password without her knowledge.The man continued stalking her. She saw him following her and their son on various occasions and reported these incidents. He jogged through her neighbourhood, although he had never done so during the marriage. He waited at a coffee shop she often visited, followed her in his car and hid in bushes to watch her. He also left anonymous packages and showed up at their son’s sporting events.The husband was charged with three counts of violating the no-contact order. Later, he took a plea deal, and those charges were dropped. The City of Seattle subsequently charged him with stalking and ordered him to wear an electronic home monitor. The city dismissed that charge without giving a public reason.The restraining order issued during the divorce proceedings was set to expire in September 2025. That was when the husband began posting online about how he planned to ‘outlive’ his wife. The wife said the posts frightened her even more because he had been spending time with a woman who had previously been convicted of killing her husband. Fearing for her life, the woman applied for a protection order that month. She submitted police reports, court orders, her own statements from the criminal case, a domestic violence assessment and screenshots of her husband’s Facebook posts. He responded with his own documents, including messages from a co-parenting app and a transcript of her statements to police in 2021.After hearing both sides in November 2025, a court commissioner issued the order, which protects her until 25 November 2030. However, the husband had shown no intention of complying with the order. The commissioner found that he had violated the no-contact order three times and continued watching his wife after the criminal case had ended. He had never completed a court-ordered domestic violence programme. A superior court judge denied his request to reconsider the decision and adopted the order as the court’s own.The appeal and outcomeThe husband appealed. He argued that he had moved out of state, that the court needed special evidence to justify a five-year order and that the judge had ignored his evidence challenging his wife’s credibility.In a ruling issued on November 9, 2026, the Washington Court of Appeals, Division One, rejected each argument. The court said state law does not allow a judge to deny an order because the person named in it has moved away. It also said the law does not require a special type of evidence to determine how long an order should last. Appellate courts do not reweigh credibility, and the judge had confirmed that he reviewed the full record, including the husband’s written arguments.The court also found a serious problem with the husband’s brief: he had cited a case that does not exist. The court refused to consider arguments based on that citation and awarded his wife attorney fees for the appeal, describing his filings as largely unsupported.The ruling is unpublished, which means other courts in Washington are not bound by it. Nevertheless, it confirms that the protection order will remain in place until 2030 and that the husband’s move out of state did not change the outcome.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US petrol prices are down, but elevated inflation continues
articles.summary: Inflation has remained high, despite some easing in fuel prices caused by the US war on Iran.
articles.body:
Consumer prices in the United States increased in October more than expected, even as petrol prices fell to a four-month low after some easing of concerns about the long-term impact of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz on global markets.

In its latest report released on Tuesday, the US Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for all items rose by 0.4 percent in October, continuing an inflationary trend since July. The average cost of shelter, as well as food, also rose in October, according to the agency.

The Labor Department’s report was higher than the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, which had forecast the CPI to increase by 0.2 percent, and economists polled by FactSet, who had predicted an increase of 0.3 percent, despite the lowering pressure on energy prices.

On Monday, US President Donald Trump said that future military action against Tehran was unlikely. “Iran militarily is effectively over,” Trump said. “We’re just keeping it the status quo, and we’re doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours.”

The average price of a gallon of petrol fell below $4 ($1.06 per litre) for the first time since July, according to the American Automobile Association. But the average price, currently $3.98, is still significantly higher than the $3.07 mark it was at a year ago. The average price of a gallon of petrol was $2.98 ($0.78 per litre) on February 28, when the US and Israel first struck Iran.

The economy and cost-of-living concerns were leading concerns for voters in midterm elections that were held on November 3, which saw Republicans lose control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate. A Reuters/Ipsos poll released on the eve of the elections found that 78 percent of voters said cost-of-living was very important or the most important issue for them when considering how they would vote. Democrats, the poll found, were favoured by 43 percent of voters, compared with 32 percent who preferred Republicans to handle it.

How voters view Trump himself has also turned largely negative since the war and its impact on the economy. Only 32 percent of voters approved of his job performance, according to the Reuters/Ipsos poll, just one point above his record low of 31 percent last month.

Trump’s Republican Party was dealt major losses in the midterm elections, losing typically Republican seats in Congress in states like Texas and Kansas.

Trump himself, as well as key members of his administration like Vice President JD Vance, have acknowledged that the war on Iran played a part in those electoral losses.
