articles.title: Botley West solar farm refused planning permission
articles.summary: Harm to greenbelt land and "adverse impacts on aviation safety” are among the reasons.
articles.body:
Plans to build a controversial £800m solar farm have been refused by the government.

The 840MW Botley West in Oxfordshire would have spread across more than 2,000 acres of land to the north and west of Oxford.

But Baroness Margaret Curran, on behalf of the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero, said "substantial" harm would be caused to greenbelt and heritage assets, as well as negative impacts on the landscape.

John Orme from the group Stop Botley West said the news had "restored a bit of faith" in the planning process. Developer Photovolt Development Partners (PVDP) has been approached for a comment.

The decision follows several years of consultations and has been postponed twice , giving the government more time to "consider further information".

Development consent was also refused as the site would have "adverse impacts on aviation safety" presenting an unacceptable risk to public safety.

Oxfordshire is home to several flying schools and London Oxford Airport.

PVDP previously said the project was crucial to meet the UK's climate and energy security goals, and could power the equivalent of 330,000 homes.

The company has six weeks to launch a judicial review.

Orme said the campaign group "has always said that we have a great enthusiasm for the use of solar".

"We really would like solar more on roofs, on brownfield sites, on industrial sites," he said.

"We've spent a lot of time with a lot of farmers who are actually putting real value back into that land and to have that finally recognised by the government ... [is] absolute delight."

He added campaigners would "continue to use every communication means we can" to object if a judicial review was pursued.

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

Trade body Solar Energy UK said it was "disappointed and surprised".

"This is a regrettable decision. We all know the desperate need for cheaper power and to push expensive gas off the grid – and that's exactly what solar farms deliver," chief executive Chris Hewett said.

Solar Energy UK said it would have also offered benefits such as allotments and jobs, as well as "extensive areas of new native woodland, wildflower meadows and greenways".

West Oxfordshire District Council had raised "significant concerns about the proposal, including its impact on the landscape and rural character".

Lib Dem Liz Leffman, executive member for planning and infrastructure, said: "We have always recognised the important role renewable energy has to play in tackling climate change and achieving net zero.

"However, we have also maintained that developments of this scale must be planned carefully and must appropriately balance national energy needs with protecting local communities, our countryside, heritage and natural environment."

Calum Miller, Lib Dem MP for Bicester and Woodstock, had previously called for the application to be refused and praised the government for listening.

"This is the right decision for our area, and enormous credit belongs to the local campaigners and councils who worked tirelessly to make their case," he said.

"Developers must take their responsibilities seriously and work with communities to deliver renewable energy that earns their support."

articles.title: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.summary: Joe Biden was in Dublin to see his son Hunter awarded the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse
articles.body:
At least two arrests have been made following a surprise visit from former US President Joe Biden to Trinity College in Dublin on Tuesday.

Biden was accompanied by former first lady Jill Biden as they attended a ceremony where their son Hunter was awarded the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse.

During the trio's visit to the College Historical Society groups of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered, some of whom were detained by gardaí (Irish police).

As Biden and his family left the venue, some of the people moved forward and objects were thrown, Irish broadcaster RTÉ has reported.

A number of garda officers and public order unit vans were on site as at least two arrests were made.

In 2024 Hunter Biden was convicted of gun and tax crimes in in the US but was later pardoned by his father while he was still president .

It made him the first child of a sitting president to be a convicted of a crime.

Previous recipients of the award include former Irish president Michael D Higgins, Bob Geldof, Patti Smith, Julian Assange and Desmond Tutu.

The former US president and his family also met with the Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin.

Martin said on X that he had been pleased to welcome the family and that they reflected on Biden's "strong Irish roots".

No flights had arrived at Jersey Airport since 09:24 GMT, although a plane from London Gatwick did land at Guernsey Airport at 17:26.

articles.title: Trump administration again boycotts UN human rights review
articles.summary: UN Human Rights Council delays US human rights record examination until January after Washington refuses meeting.
articles.body:
The United States ⁠⁠has again boycotted a United Nations examination of its human rights record, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations under President Donald Trump are surging to levels not seen in decades.

US representatives on Tuesday failed to show up at the UN in Geneva for the review, which all 193 UN member states undergo every four to five years.

“The delegation of the United States is not present in the room,” UN Human Rights Council President Sidharto Reza Suryodipuro, of Indonesia, announced as the session was set to begin.

The US refusal to participate prompted the UN body to delay examining the US human rights record until January. This is the second year in a row that Washington has skipped its own review.

The US withdrew from the council in February 2025 shortly after Trump began his second presidential term, claiming it was biased against Israel.

The Trump administration has been a fierce critic of the UN, withdrawing Washington from key agencies, slashing its funding and bypassing the body in launching the war on Iran.

A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the council’s work.

“[We] give no credibility to the agency,” the spokesperson said.

“This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own ‘values’ as it pushes anti-American rhetoric,” the official added, without responding to allegations about the US record.

The 47-member council has not directly criticised Washington’s rights record. However, experts have expressed alarm over issues such as migrant deportations, which Washington maintains are carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

UN documents show countries had planned to raise issues such as abortion access and the death penalty.

US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering ⁠⁠topics from migration to racial discrimination.

“Enough is enough,” Jamil Dakwar, of the American Civil Liberties Union, told ⁠⁠reporters in Geneva.

“We’ve seen attacks on fundamental human rights and civil liberties unprecedented in generations,” he added.

Fourteen countries are due to take part in ⁠⁠the review process in Geneva this month. During Trump’s first term in office, the US submitted its UN Universal Periodic Review (UPR) report.

Eric Tistounet, a visiting professor at the Geneva Graduate Institute who was the council’s first secretary, said the US walkout could affect the credibility of the council’s review system.

“If the predominant global power, which has always claimed to adhere to the human rights norms, doesn’t show up and doesn’t even justify why, then you are in big trouble,” he said.

articles.title: 1MDB: Malaysia's disgraced former PM Najib Razak leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
articles.summary: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.
articles.body:
Malaysia's disgraced former Prime Minister Najib Razak has arrived home to begin serving the rest of a jail sentence for corruption under house arrest.

There was a big media presence at his Kuala Lumpur residence to see the 73-year-old return from prison in an SUV late on Tuesday night, escorted by a heavily armed police convoy.

Najib's return ended a four-year prison stint after he was found guilty over the embezzlement of billions of dollars from the country's sovereign wealth fund.

The 1MDB scandal brought down his government and made headlines around the world when it came to light a decade ago, embroiling prominent figures from Malaysia to Goldman Sachs and Hollywood.

Investigators estimated that $4.5bn (£3.3bn) was siphoned from the state-owned wealth fund, which Najib co-founded, into private pockets, including his own. More than $1bn allegedly ended up in accounts linked to Najib, according to prosecutors.

Najib's lawyers claim he had been misled by his advisers - in particular the financier Jho Low, who has maintained his innocence and remains at large.

Najib's mansion in one of the capital's most exclusive neighbourhoods was declared a federal prison ahead of his homecoming on Tuesday.

Critics said his release from jail undermined efforts to fight corruption and questioned its legal basis, saying Malaysian law made no provision for house arrest.

Najib, who was prime minister from 2009 to 2018, denied wrongdoing but was convicted at two separate trials.

In the first trial he was sentenced in 2020 to 12 years in prison and jailed in 2022. The term was later halved on appeal.

In September, the King of Malaysia granted him a conditional pardon to see out the remaining two years of his sentence at home.

The transfer to his mansion was to take place on Friday but put on hold after the attorney general sought clarification of the royal decree. On Tuesday the high court ruled the house arrest was effective immediately.

Najib's party paid a $12m fine as part of the terms of the royal pardon allowing him to serve the rest of his term at home.

He was sentenced after being convicted of abuse of power, money laundering and breach of trust over 42 million ringgit ($10m; £7.7m) transferred from SRC International - a former unit of 1MDB - into his private accounts.

Najib is appealing against a 15-year prison sentence, handed down at a second trial in December 2025 , in a case involving much larger sums of money. In that case he was convicted of misappropriating nearly 2.3 billion Malaysian ringgit ($569m; £422m) from the nation's sovereign wealth fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).

He is due to start serving that sentence after his house arrest ends, which is expected in August 2028.

articles.title: Ole Miss student apologizes for alleged racist taunts in viral doorbell video
articles.summary: The university said it is investigating the incident.
articles.body:
One of the female University of Mississippi students caught in camera footage outside of a Black student's apartment Friday evening allegedly making racist noises and gestures apologized for her behavior on Tuesday.

"To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize," the student said in a statement released by a representative on her behalf. "Before the incident on November 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however, I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful."

Two of the three women in the video, which was posted to TikTok, are seen briefly stepping toward the door camera, beating their chests while grunting and cooing like monkeys. The video had been viewed over 12.5 million times as of early Tuesday afternoon.

"I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color," the student said in her statement. "I have apologized to the women and I pray they will forgive me. I can never truly understand the pain I have caused them and it was never my intention. These girls deserve to feel seen and understood and what I did is not a reflection of who I am trying to become."

"[T]he incident is being actively investigated by the appropriate university offices," University of Mississippi Vice Chancellor Shawnboda Mead said in a statement Monday, in part, adding, "our staff have reached out to the students directly impacted to offer support, listen to their concerns, and connect them with available resources. We will continue to support them as we work through this process."

"I understand the seriousness of this situation and remain committed to taking responsibility and learning from this embarrassing ordeal," the student's statement said, adding that she "intend[s] to cooperate fully with the university's investigation."

articles.title: UK children’s author David Walliams accused of grooming minors
articles.summary: A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News details allegations made by multiple women against the 55-year-old.
articles.body:
British comedian and children’s author David Walliams, 55, has been accused of grooming teenage fans and sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl at his house, according to British media outlets.

The Guardian newspaper and ITV News broadcaster published a joint investigation on Tuesday into allegations by multiple women who gave firsthand accounts of Walliams’s alleged misconduct.

Walliams denied targeting teenagers and using his fame to manipulate them to have sex, his lawyers told the media.

Walliams said he “behaved thoughtlessly” in a letter addressing journalists, which was published by The Guardian.

“I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me,” he wrote.

Walliams is best known for starring in the BBC’s popular “Little Britain” sketch show in the early 2000s.

He authored more than 40 books, including “Mr. Stink”, “Gangsta Granny” and “The Boy in the Dress”, with his work translated into more than 50 languages and reportedly selling 50 million copies.

He was also a judge on ITV’s “Britain’s Got Talent” for years but stepped down in 2022 after apologising for making “disrespectful comments” about auditioning contestants.

Following ITV News and The Guardian’s investigation, the BBC said it was removing some programmes and would conduct a review of “all material featuring and written by David Walliams on our platforms”.

Last year, his publisher, HarperCollins, dropped him after he faced accusations of harassing young female colleagues, which he denied.

He sought a court injunction to prevent ITV News and The Guardian from identifying him in their reporting but was blocked by a UK High Court judge last week.

Walliams’s lawyer, Sara Mansoori, told the court he had made an attempt on his life when he received letters from the publications seeking his response to the allegations. She said he later made another attempt, and he was admitted to hospital for psychiatric care last month.

A summary of the court judgement stated that some of the alleged conduct could amount to criminal offences if proven.

Nearly all the women alleging sexual misconduct by Walliams were identified only by first names.

A woman named as “Jade” said Walliams, then aged 36, contacted her through a social media page showing her age as 15 and invited her to his house in 2007. She accused him of “sexual assault” and “grooming”.

Walliams’s lawyers denied sexual contact with Jade.

A woman named as “Alex” told The Guardian that he first met her when she was a 15-year-old aspiring comedy writer and he was 32. She alleged that they engaged in sexual conduct for the first time at his home when she was 17 and he was 34.

“I think I was groomed, 100 percent. We met when I was 15, and he was promising to help me,” she said.

It is illegal in the UK for someone older than 18 to intentionally communicate with a child younger than 16 for a sexual purpose. Walliams’s lawyers told The Guardian he believed Alex was 18.

articles.title: Denmark’s Aarhus is building a 110 MW geothermal heating system, with three facilities expected to meet 20% of the city’s district heating demand
articles.summary: A geothermal heating project in Aarhus, Denmark, is moving towards a three-facility system designed to provide a substantial share of the city’s district
articles.body: A geothermal heating project in Aarhus, Denmark, is moving towards a three-facility system designed to provide a substantial share of the city’s district heating. The first plant at Skejby began supplying heat to local homes on 31 October 2025, while construction and drilling work continue at other sites. The completed system is planned to have a total capacity of 110 megawatts and meet 20% of Aarhus’ district heating demand.The project is intended to operate for at least 30 years once completed and fully operational. According to Innargi (2025), the three facilities are expected to be completed in 2029, following an optimisation that reduced the planned number of locations from seven. Innargi is working with district heating company Kredsløb.How does the Aarhus geothermal system connect underground heat to city homesThe project is being developed by Innargi in collaboration with Kredsløb, the district heating company in Aarhus. The system is planned to comprise three facilities across the city by 2030. One is already operating at Skejby, where the first geothermal heat entered the district heating network in October 2025. Drilling has commenced at the Port of Aarhus site, while the third plant is planned.Once fully built out, the three-site project is expected to be the largest integrated geothermal district heating system in the European Union. The facilities will transfer heat from a geothermal reservoir to the city’s district heating network, supplying heat to connected homes.How did new technology help optimise Aarhus’ geothermal heating projectThe project’s exploration phase included the drilling and evaluation of three test wells between 2023 and 2024. According to Innargi, the results confirmed a strong geothermal resource beneath the city. The company also said improvements in technology during the project’s first year helped optimise the plan. Instead of developing the seven locations originally planned, the project will deliver the same heat from three locations.The revised approach forms the basis of the system being developed in Aarhus. The three facilities are planned across the city, including Skejby and the Port of Aarhus. The first facility at Skejby is already supplying heat, while work on the remaining facilities is continuing. The exploration work provided information used to assess the underground geothermal resource.Aarhus geothermal plants set to meet 20% of the city’s district heating demandThe planned combined capacity of the geothermal heating plants is 110 megawatts. According to Innargi, this would equal 20% of Aarhus’ district heating demand. The figure refers specifically to the city’s district heating demand, rather than all energy use across Aarhus. The company expects the three facilities to be completed in 2029.The facilities are expected to operate for at least 30 years. The system is designed to draw heat from the geothermal resource below the city and transfer it into the existing district heating network. Its planned capacity is intended to make geothermal energy a significant part of the city’s heat supply.From exploration to heat supply: Aarhus geothermal project advances in stagesInnargi’s project timeline lists preparations for the exploration phase in 2022, followed by exploration and appraisal between 2022 and 2025. Delivery of the first heat was scheduled for 2025, and the first Skejby facility began supplying the network in October that year. Construction of the remaining facilities is scheduled for 2026 to 2029.The company says the three facilities are expected to be completed in 2029, provided the project proceeds as planned.You use AI every day. articles.title: Person has no claim in grandpa's property held by dad, says SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Can a grandson claim a share in property inherited by his father from his grandfather?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Can a grandson claim a share in property inherited by his father from his grandfather? Supreme Court has ruled that a person becomes the absolute owner of his share in his father's ancestral or self-acquired property and can deal with it exclusively, including excluding his sons.Ending a 29-year legal battle, a bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and Sunita Agarwal rejected a son's plea for partition of his father's property. The son had filed the suit in 1997, claiming the property was ancestral or joint family property. The court said a son's son is not listed as a Class I heir under the Hindu Succession Act and cannot claim a share in his grandfather's property.Referring to Section 8, which lays down succession rules when a Hindu male dies intestate, the bench said a son becomes the absolute owner of property inherited from his father, while his own son has no right by birth over it.SC said Class I heirs inherit simultaneously, to the exclusion of all others. "A son's son is not mentioned as an heir under Class I of the Schedule, and, therefore, he could not get any right in the property of his grandfather," it said.It added that 1956 law did not preserve right under personal Hindu law of a grandson to claim a share in his grandfather's property during his father's lifetime. Sec 8 must be read as a self-contained provision governing devolution of property of a Hindu male dying intestate, it said.Citing SC judgements, the bench rejected the argument that a son inheriting property under Section 8 holds it as karta of his undivided family. Such an interpretation would create two classes among Class I heirs, treating property as joint family property for male heirs but not female heirs, it said. The express wording of Sec 8 must prevail.Upholding HC's order, the bench said a grandson cannot seek partition of property held by his father. The high court had ruled that when a son or daughter receives property through partition, whether ancestral or self-acquired, they become absolute owners of their shares and can deal with them exclusively, including excluding their sons.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Tesla found liable for fraud over $110,000 Solar Roof that never generated electricity; project began at $82,210 in 2020, failed county inspection, homeowner estimates repair cost at $2.5 million
articles.summary: A California judge has found Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation in a lawsuit involving a Solar Roof installation that was never
articles.body: A California judge has found Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation in a lawsuit involving a Solar Roof installation that was never completed and failed to generate electricity for the homeowner. The ruling follows repeated disputes over the company's failure to produce documents sought during the legal proceedings.The case concerns Ambrose Conroy, a resident of Rancho Santa Fe, California, who signed an agreement with Tesla in March 2020 for a Solar Roof system worth $82,210. However, the project's cost increased to approximately $110,000 after two amendments by February 2021. The revised installation was to include an 18.2-kilowatt roof and six Powerwall batteries.According to a report by Electrek, the roof was never completed, did not pass a county inspection and never generated a single kilowatt-hour of electricity for Conroy's home. The homeowner estimates that repairing the damage could cost more than $2.5 million. Tesla had reportedly offered him $5,000 to settle the dispute in April 2022.Why the California judge found Tesla liable for fraudThe lawsuit, known as Conroy v. Tesla, was filed in 2022 in the North County division of the San Diego Superior Court. Judge Cynthia Freeland had previously sanctioned Tesla twice over its failure to provide documents during the discovery process.The company was ordered to pay $15,467.50 in February 2026 and another $13,500 in June. The judge had warned that further failures could lead to issue sanctions, under which disputed facts could be treated as established.After Tesla missed another deadline, the court ruled on September 11 that the company was liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation. The decision meant that the remaining proceedings on those claims would focus on determining compensatory and punitive damages.The missing material reportedly included Microsoft Teams messages, workplace safety records, emails with San Diego County inspectors and more than 20 quality, installation and safety reports from Tesla's internal system.Tesla subsequently asked Judge Freeland to reconsider the ruling, arguing that it had produced the relevant documents. However, in an October 27 decision, the judge rejected the request. According to Electrek, she said the late-produced documents could support Conroy's argument that Tesla knowingly used his home as an experiment despite lacking the experience needed to deliver the promised installation.Internal Tesla messages reportedly described the project as an experimentThe case has also drawn attention to internal communications involving senior Tesla employees. According to the trial exhibit list reviewed by Electrek, one exhibit refers to text messages dated January 13, 2021, involving Bobby Yang, Tesla's director of model engineering, and other employees. Conroy's legal team has cited the messages in support of its claim that the company was experimenting with the installation.Electrek clarified that it had not independently seen the text messages themselves and that the description came from the exhibit list submitted by Conroy's side.The publication also reported on internal emails quoted in the complaint. In one exchange from February 2021, Yang reportedly described Conroy's house as being in the 99.5th percentile in terms of complexity. RJ Johnson, who was then heading Tesla's energy business, reportedly acknowledged that the project could affect the company's numbers but said it needed to make things right.The case also refers to daily progress reports being sent to CEO Elon Musk, who is listed as a witness by Conroy's legal team.Homeowner describes damaged tiles and prolonged installation workConroy's lawsuit also details the problems he says his family experienced during the installation. The removal of the existing roof, which was expected to take two days, reportedly took two weeks. The complaint alleges that parts of the roof were left exposed for extended periods and that scratched and damaged tiles were installed.Some glass tiles allegedly shattered around the driveway and lawn, with the family claiming that the broken pieces made it unsafe to walk barefoot in the area.The legal dispute continued even after the initial installation problems. In February 2025, Tesla reportedly failed another San Diego County inspection after arriving without the required plans for the venting system.Conroy also hired an electrical consultant to examine the installation. According to the consultant's assessment cited in the reporting, the wiring and conduits beneath the tiles could increase the risk of a short circuit and fire during heavy rain. Tesla's lawyers disputed the characterisation of the fire risk, according to Electrek.Conroy is now in the process of removing the roof.Tesla challenges the ruling as the legal battle continuesTesla has continued to contest the fraud and negligent misrepresentation findings. In an October 29 filing, the company asked the court to freeze the case while it seeks relief from the California Court of Appeal. Tesla argued that the sanction was unduly punitive, violated due process and effectively amounted to a directed verdict on fraud before a trial.The company had separately stipulated to liability on three other claims in the lawsuit: breach of contract, breach of warranty and negligence. It had continued to contest the remaining two claims until the judge's September ruling.The case is still ongoing, and Conroy has not yet been awarded the compensation he is seeking. The November 20 trial date has been vacated, with a trial-readiness conference scheduled for December 4, according to Electrek.Tesla's Solar Roof was introduced in 2016 by Elon Musk as a roofing option designed to combine solar technology with the appearance of conventional premium roof tiles. The Conroy case has brought renewed scrutiny to the company's installation practices and the challenges surrounding the product.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: No. 2 Duke faces No. 5 Michigan State in State Farm Champions Classic showdown tonight
articles.summary: College basketball's State Farm Champions Classic pits No. 5 Michigan State against No. 2 Duke tonight at Chicago's United Center in a top-5 clash.
articles.body: College Basketball has returned to action this season, and while most schools are playing inferior opponents, we do finally have a few ranked matchups. This is pretty much what happens every season. Most schools play lower-level clubs so they can get some easy wins out of the way, figure out their offense, and make adjustments before the Thanksgiving tournaments. Tonight, we have the State Farm Champions Classic, featuring two of the best in the country: Michigan State vs. Duke. Michigan State comes into the game with a ranking of fifth in the nation, and at least part of that is due to its returning players. Jeremy Fears Jr. has been one of the better guards in college sports and is the catalyst for this team. He makes this team go, and in two games, he has led the team in scoring. It isn't much scoring at just 12 points per game, but either way, he still leads the team. Coen Carr is an athletic forward who thrives on defense and rebounding. articles.title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, cut off his ankle monitor, DOJ says
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials.
articles.body: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials. Markle was arrested on Friday after officials found child sexual abuse images in storage units belonging to him in California, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with minors, the Justice Department said. He was taken into custody in Tampa, Florida, where he was released under house arrest. He allegedly cut off his ankle monitor at 1:45 a.m. Tuesday, U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Tuesday. “We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law,” Essayli said. FBI investigators found slides, film negatives, and books that contained “suspected child pornography” in two storage units rented by Markle in Los Angeles, according to court documents. The film negatives including images of naked “pre-pubescent” girls with an adult male, who a witness positively identified as Markle, the FBI said. One unit had mail bearing the name Thomas Markle and an international driver’s permit with his name, birthdate and a photo appearing to be him, according to a criminal complaint. Markle’s storage rentals date as far back as the summer of 2008, the complaint said. The seizure last week came weeks after news that an investigation was opened into Markle in the Philippines over allegations that he kept similar images at his home while living there. There were thousands of photos featuring “underage male and females” recovered, authorities said. Markle has been living in a senior care facility in Florida, according to The Associated Press. He was reportedly forced to return to the U.S. after living in Philippines after he suffered a stroke a leg was amputated. A judge ordered an independent psychological evaluation to see if Markle was fit to stand trial. The order noted Markle’s health condition, age and lack of recall as reasonable cause to believe he may have some mental “disease or defect” that would render him mentally incompetent. Markle has denied the allegations, describing the accusations as “sick lies.” An attorney for Markle in court records for Markle did not immediately return a request for comment from NBC News on Tuesday. A spokesperson for the Prince Harry and Meghan declined to comment on the arrest last week. Last month, Meghan revealed that she had been made aware of allegations against her father years ago. She said in a statement that she was “deeply disturbed” by the allegations and that her relationship has been limited with him over the years. He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, which was the subject of widespread media scrutiny. Meghan said she has also chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father for their protection. “The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” she said. British police confirmed that Meghan was passed a letter in January 2019 which contained “a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.” London’s Metropolitan Police referred itself to the country’s policing watchdog over the handling of the allegations, saying it had not informed other law enforcement agencies of the allegations.

articles.title: Lola blanket vs. Comfrt vs. Cocoon: Which brand makes the best plush blanket?
articles.summary: I tested three of the best, ultra-soft plush blankets from Lola Blankets, Comfrt and Cocoon, to see which is the best all around.
articles.body: When it comes to bedding, it’s fair to say that many people take their fitted sheets, comforters, duvets and pillows very seriously, and rightfully so. In a world where everyone you know is moving a million miles a minute, sleep can be scarce, so investing in ultra-luxe bedding to help get some rest isn’t all that outlandish. One area of bedding that’s had a seemingly meteoric rise recently is plush blankets. These soft, faux fur throws have become a go-to for anyone fixated on achieving ultimate comfort, whether that’s at home, or in my case, in a chilly office. However you’ve come to familiarize yourself with this category, you may have noticed that there are a few brands that have become household names (both figuratively and literally): Lola Blankets, Comfrt and Cocoon. While Lola and Cocoon specialize in plush blankets, available in several sizes, colors, weights and patterns (and have collaborations with brands like LoveShackFancy and Maisonette), Comfrt is primarily an athleisure apparel brand, known for its popular hoodies and crewnecks, that has recently emerged as a frontrunner in the cozy blanket race. So naturally, our team at NBC Selected decided to try all three. To see which of these plush blankets is the best, I tested each of them for three weeks. I judged them based on features like softness, warmth, weight and more. Below, I talk more about where they each excel and fall short, and which one I think offers the best value. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. How I tested the Lola, Comfrt and Cocoon blankets Lola, Comfrt and Cocoon each sent me a blanket for the purpose of testing. Since I get very cold in the office, I decided it would be a great idea to test the blankets while working at my desk, where I thought I’d get the most use from the blankets. I paid attention to softness, weight, warmth, foldability, storability and slipperiness (no one likes that blanket that’s constantly falling off the back of the couch). I mainly wore each of the blankets around my upper body, including my shoulders, a few times each week, while sitting at my desk. Softness: Out of the box, I found the Lola blanket to be notably the softest. While all the blankets have an amazing silky texture, the Lola blanket felt extremely cozy, slightly more so than the two others. With that said, the Comfrt blanket has the fluffiest texture and the Cocoon blanket excels in its weight, which I explain more below. Warmth: I tried the blankets consecutively as I received them and wanted to test them all in the office because the temperature is often cold but consistent and I wanted to standardize the environment. In terms of overall warmth, I found all of the blankets to be relatively warm, though I found Cocoon the warmest largely due to its weighty feel. Slipperiness: Sometimes, when bedding is so soft (like a silk sheet or pillowcase), it can naturally slide off of your body. If you don’t move around a lot, this probably isn’t much of an issue for you, but it’s something I considered. When I wasn’t actively wearing the blankets, I draped each one on the back of my chair, which also proved to be a great testing strategy because some of the blankets tend to be very slippery. While they all mostly stayed in place, I tend to move around a lot in my seat (similar to when I sleep), so sometimes each of the blankets would slide off the chair or make me slide partially off my chair. Storability and foldability: When I finally had all of the blankets at once, I stored the ones I wasn’t using in the drawers next to my desk. This gave me a chance to test the foldability of each of the blankets. All of them are relatively fluffy, so none of them really fold perfectly like a shirt or flat sheet, though I found that the Lola folded the easiest and most flat compared to the Comfrt and Cocoon blankets. Since the Lola was the easiest to fold, I found that it was also the easiest to store in the drawers. Weight: In terms of weight, all of the blankets had a great amount of heft to them, even though they weren’t the weighted versions of the blankets. Of all the blankets, the Cocoon had the most weighted feel, though I’m personally neutral about weighted blankets overall. The softest blanket I tested the Lola Original blanket, which is one of the brand’s bestselling blankets. It’s available in almost 100 colors and patterns, including jewel-tones, animal prints and stars. Lola blankets are made from a mix of polyester and spandex. This blanket has a sort of bubbly knit texture, which is common in all of the blankets I tested and something I love since it provides added plushness compared to a flat blanket. Plus, it has a zero-shed design, which after testing, I can verify is true — I didn’t get any small pieces of fabric or pilling on my clothing or chair at work. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans has washed and air dried her two Lola blankets at least a dozen times and she says they’ve never shed and haven’t lost their softness. Additionally, NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio is equally in love with her three Lola Blankets, which she also says are unbelievably soft. It was the most foldable of all the blankets, and fit inside my large desk drawer while leaving room for a tote and a few small pieces of necessary office supplies. As someone who lives in a small apartment, I appreciate how well it stores for its large size. And it has weight to it — not so much that I felt like I was being suffocated, but enough to keep me warm for hours and to keep it from slipping off my chair constantly. What I loved most about the Lola Original blanket, though, and what I think is its most notable feature, is how incredibly soft it is — it is the softest of all the blankets I tested, the texture was the ost buttery and silk-like. I had multiple people on staff stop by my desk just to ask if they could feel the texture and they were all very impressed. I loved wrapping myself in the blanket, and even after wearing it for more than an hour at a time in the office, I didn’t get overheated or start to sweat, which is a problem for me as someone who runs hot. The fluffiest blanket My introduction to Comfrt was through its popular Signature Hoodie, which I still wear regularly and love because of how soft it is and how well it’s held up over time. Since I had such an amazing experience with Comfrt’s apparel, I was eager to try the brand’s popular Dreamer Blanket. The blanket looks very similar to Lola’s Original blanket, though I’d say the Lola has a little bit more of a bubbly texture to it. The Dreamer blanket is also incredibly soft — it has a vegan faux-fur texture that’s fluffy (it’s the furriest and had the most animal-like feel), doesn’t get matted and doesn’t shed or pill. Another great thing about the Dreamer Blanket is that it’s the closest you can get to the look and feel of the Lola Blanket, but for less money. The Lola retails for $325 for the large and the large Comfrt Dreamer costs $309 — so while it’s still pricey, it will save you a few dollars. One of the biggest differences is that the Comfrt Dreamer has a bit more weight to it than the Lola, which is ideal if you love a blanket with a slightly weighy feel. (Note: Lola Blanket does make a weighted version of its Original, but for this story I compared all non-weighted options.) The weight of this blanket fell somewhere between the others — it feels slightly heavier than the Lola, but not as weighty as the Cocoon. It was comparably soft with Lola, though it has a fluffier texture and thus is a little harder to fold neatly. Plus, I think the fluffy texture helped it slip around less compared to the others, and added to its substantial warmth. Overall, the Comfrt Dreamer Blanket delivers in all of the categories I measured (softness, comfort, warmth and weight), though it’s slightly less expensive than the Lola and slightly more expensive than the Cocoon blanket. If I was splitting hairs, I would say the Lola is still softer than the Comfrt blanket, but other than that (and a few more color options), I’d say they’re very similar in all major areas. The weightiest blanket Cocoon’s blanket comes in the fewest sizes and colors compared to the Lola and Comfrt. The brand sells ultra-plush blankets available in two types: classic and weighted. The blankets are given different numbers and names based on their color or style. You can shop blankets in colors that are very similar to options at Lola and Comfrt, like fawn and cream, but the brand also has striped options with names inspired by flowers, like primrose, poppy, camellia and sunflower. Just like the Lola Original and Comfrt Dreamer blanket, the Cocoon Classic is made of a poly-spandex blend and has that bubbly texture. The best feature of the Cocoon Classic blanket is the weighted feel of the traditional (non-weighted) version. If the non-weighted blanket is this substantial, I can only imagine how the actual weighted blanket feels. This is great for people who love weighted blankets and especially for those who get improved sleep from one. In fact, several of the reviews on the brand’s site note how weighted the blanket feels, describing it as a particularly positive feature. The Cocoon blanket, like the Lola and Comfrt blankets, is extremely soft, though the Lola and Comfrt were still somewhat softer by comparison. It is relatively easy to fold and store, particularly compared to the Comfrt blanket. This blanket is very warm and cozy, which I believe has more to do with its weight and less to do with its construction. It’s not a hoodie and it is soft, so it did fall off my shoulders slightly, but not to the point of annoyance. While there are many weighted blankets available today, there aren’t a ton that are plush enough to compare to the Lola and Comfrt. And at $295, it rings up as the least expensive of all the blankets I’ve tried, but not the lowest in quality. My final thoughts on the Lola, Comfrt and Cocoon blankets Lola Original Blanket This is the blanket for you if your biggest priority is softness. This was definitely the plushest in feel, and it has a fluffy and bubbly texture that works surprisingly well, even for someone like me who finds ultra-soft blankets can get too warm. With that said, it’s the most expensive option, so depending on your budget it might be for the holiday or birthday wishlist — or a big sale event. Comfrt Dreamer Blanket The Comfrt Dreamer Blanket is perfect for anyone who wants an extremely soft blanket that has a medium amount of natural weight and is also available in multiple fun colors. This blanket has a very fluffy texture, more than the Lola and Cocoon. I think of all the blankets, it has the best value for the price because it has a substantial amount of softness, weight and fluffiness without causing overheating and it slipped the least. Cocoon Classic This is the pinnacle of weighted blankets, particularly because the non-weighted option (the Classic) already has a substantial amount of natural heft to it. It’s ideal for people who love weighted blankets. If you know someone who only sleeps with one or gets cold very easily, this is one of the best options I could recommend. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home, storage and organization, among other topics. I also write reviews and brand guides for bedding brands and more. For this story, I tested plush blankets from three popular brands to find out which one was the softest and offered the best value for its price. articles.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle detained for allegedly cutting off ankle monitor, officials say
articles.summary: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
articles.body:
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been detained in Florida for allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to justice department officials in Los Angeles.

Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in Tampa after allegedly removing the monitor at 01:45 local time (06:45 GMT), a justice department (DoJ) spokesperson told the BBC.

The judge ordered him jailed without bond and he is now in federal custody, the spokesperson said.

Markle, who has previously denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.

The BBC has contacted representatives for Markle.

"Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions. We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday.

Markle was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the justice department (DoJ) said.

Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.

In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.

Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention.

He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ.

FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions".

Markle has called the allegations "sick lies".

articles.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
articles.body:
Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the affair between its chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.

Jensen Huang, a co-founder of Nvidia who has led it to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman outside of his marriage.

The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. She is an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.

Nvidia said on Tuesday that Wachtell attorney Joon Kim was set to lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into Jensen Huang's affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe.

Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the US artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools.

Shares in the company fell to a near-yearly low on Tuesday, wiping more than $500bn (£375bn) off Nvidia's stock market value since Friday, even as tech stocks have recovered since last week's sell-off.

Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive of an Nvidia customer, who is also believed by the US government to be spying for China, has business and national security implications.

According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring this year, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China".

US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoke to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him.

When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy

Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security

Joon Kim is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts.

Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce.

The investigation is expected to be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the sentiment inside Nvidia. It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang.

Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia. He has become a key public figure in the devleopment on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity.

A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any additional of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI.

articles.title: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.summary: Salvadoran troops backed the police operation ahead of the Haitian prime minister’s visit to El Salvador.
articles.body:
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele said that Salvadoran troops have targeted one of Haiti’s largest criminal organisations. It comes amid international calls to respect international human rights law.

Bukele announced the attack on Tuesday on the social media platform X.

“We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmo San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang’s headquarters,” the right-wing leader wrote.

Bukele posted a video of helicopters circling overhead and firing on the site in Croix-des-Bouquets, near Port-au-Prince.

The operation was reportedly conducted on Sunday by Haitian police with support from Salvadoran troops, and resulted in the killing of 20 people.

The announcement comes as Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aime, prepares to visit El Salvador next week to discuss the future of Salvadoran troops in his gang-plagued Caribbean nation.

Amnesty International has urged both countries to ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law, and called on them to release the agreement governing the mass deployment.

“Both governments must make public the agreement governing the deployment and explain how they oversee the deployed forces, what rules govern the use of force, to whom they are accountable, and how people can report possible violations without fear of reprisals,” Amnesty’s Americas director Ana Piquer said.

“Ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law,” she urged the leaders of the two nations.

She also called on both countries to establish “prompt, independent and impartial investigations into all allegations of human rights violations”.

“The response to gang violence must not replicate the abuses and impunity that have characterized previous interventions in Haiti,” she added.

Some 2,000 troops have been sent by El Salvador’s president to Haiti since the mid-October disappearance of four Salvadoran personnel.

The vast majority are not participating in the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) , raising concerns about their rules of engagement.

Bukele initially stated the deployment aimed at bringing home four Salvadoran GSF soldiers who went missing during an ambush attack on October 18.

But more recently, he has hinted at a broader goal of eliminating Haiti’s powerful gangs, as he did in his own country with a campaign pockmarked with allegations of human rights abuses.

Haiti is set to hold elections in July and October next year, marking its first ones in more than a decade.

articles.title: Devotees throng Govardhan for puja, parikrama
articles.summary: Lakhs thronged Govardhan in Mathura for Govardhan Puja and Annakoot, with 21-km parikrama, special rituals, and 10,000 foreign devotees attending.
articles.body: Lucknow: Lakhs of devotees thronged Govardhan in Mathura on Tuesday for Govardhan Puja and Annakoot Mahotsav, with the 21-km parikrama route witnessing massive footfall and temples across the Braj region hosting special rituals.The ceremonial milk abhishek of Giriraj Maharaj began before dawn at major shrines, including Daan Ghati, Mukut Mukharvind and Jatipura Mukharvind and continued through the day. Devotees undertook the traditional seven-kos parikrama, while community feasts, cultural programmes and Annakoot offerings marked the celebrations.A major attraction this year was the participation of over 10,000 foreign devotees from nearly 40 countries, many of whom joined kirtans and religious processions organised by ISKCON and Gaudiya groups. Giriraj Maharaj was offered Panchamrit and Chhappan Bhog as part of the rituals.Festivities were also held in Barsana, where devotees offered prayers at the Radha Rani temple and performed traditional Govardhan Puja rituals. Temples and homes were illuminated, while special programmes were organised at Rangeeli Mahal and Maan Garh Dham.Grand Annakoot celebrations were held at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi, Banke Bihari Temple and ISKCON temples. The Banke Bihari Temple witnessed an exceptionally heavy rush, with devotee queues stretching nearly three kilometres. articles.title: Iran-backed terror suspects plotted attack on US troops using vans packed with fuel, DOJ says
articles.summary: A Justice Department indictment alleges three Iran-backed suspects used fuel-laden vans to target RAF Fairford, a British base housing U.S. troops.
articles.body: Three suspected Iran-backed terrorists plotted an attack on a British air base housing American troops using vans carrying barrels of fuel, according to a federal indictment unsealed Tuesday by the Justice Department (DOJ). The eight-count superseding indictment charges Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali Al-Hassani with terrorism-related offenses tied to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Kata'ib Hizballah. Prosecutors say the suspects targeted RAF Fairford in England, where U.S. military aircraft and personnel were stationed. "Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American service members will be prosecuted by the United States government," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a news release. IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY According to the indictment, Al-Hassani directed associates in the United Kingdom to conduct surveillance of RAF Fairford in August, paying one individual to record video of the base's perimeter. The suspects' associates later obtained three vans and barrels of fuel, researched chemical accelerants and purchased metal objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel, prosecutors said. They also disguised the vans with commercial decals to resemble vehicles belonging to fuel delivery and swimming pool supply businesses. On Sept. 26, Al-Hassani allegedly directed associates to drive the three vans toward the base. At least two encountered a security roadblock and were unable to proceed. British authorities recovered all three vehicles and arrested their occupants the following morning. UK POLICE ARREST 'EXPLOSIVE' SUSPECTS NEAR US AIRBASE, KEY TO IRAN WAR Prosecutors allege Al-Saadi helped coordinate the operation while imprisoned in New York awaiting trial on separate terrorism charges, using telephone calls with family members in Iraq to relay coded messages to his co-conspirators. During a Sept. 24 call, Al-Saadi allegedly asked about Al-Hassani and instructed relatives to "give him [al-Hassani] money so we can do it." The alleged plot followed a series of attacks across Europe in March and April that prosecutors say the defendants helped organize on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network. Those attacks targeted synagogues, Jewish organizations, ambulances and an Israeli embassy, and included the stabbing of two Jewish men in London. Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian Iraqi national, was arrested abroad in May and transferred to U.S. custody. Prosecutors previously accused him of helping direct approximately 18 attacks in Europe and attempting to coordinate an attack on a Manhattan synagogue. Some charges carry a maximum sentence of life in prison.
